questions.q: According to this lesson, what three things should a one-minute interview answer about the capstone include?
options: The total line count, the programming language, and the file names
Only a list of every method name
The exact salary you expect to earn from this skill
What it does, the hardest decision made, and how you proved it works
questions.explain: The lesson recommends a concise structure: what the project does, the hardest design decision, and the evidence (tests) that it works.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a portfolio reviewer is most likely to actually read?
options: Every single line of source code
Only the commit history
A short README and a skim of the tests
Nothing — reviewers never look at portfolio projects
questions.explain: Reviewers typically don't read every line of code; a clear README and a glance at the tests do most of the communicating.

questions.q: What was the purpose of Chapters 1 and 2, according to this lesson's recap?
options: They were unrelated filler material
To teach REST and JSON fundamentals so Chapter 3's real AI API shapes would already make sense
To directly teach AI model internals
To replace the need for Chapter 3 entirely
questions.explain: The recap explicitly frames Chapters 1-2 as the foundation that made Chapter 3's real JSON shapes immediately readable.

questions.q: What is the next course in the AI Engineer path after this one?
options: Generative AI and LLMs
Prompt and Context Engineering
RAG and Vector Databases
AI/ML Foundations
questions.explain: Per the AI Engineer path's course order, AI/ML Foundations comes directly after APIs & JSON for AI Applications.

questions.q: What should the README's 'run the tests' section actually contain?
options: A vague description with no exact command
The exact command someone else would run to execute the test suite themselves (e.g. pytest tests/)
A link to an unrelated project
The full source code of every test
questions.explain: The lesson is specific: the README should give the exact command to run the tests, not just a general description.
